blocks.title: Formulation of the result
blocks.content: We consider the germ of an isolated hypersurface singularity $D\subseteq(\mathbb{C}^n,0)$. Let $\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{C}^n,0}$ be the ring of germs of holomorphic functions on $\mathbb{C}^n$ at the origin with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ and $f\in\mathfrak{m}^2$ a reduced defining equation of $D$. For notational simplicity, we shall write $\mathbb{C}^n$ instead of $(\mathbb{C}^n,0)$. In terms of coordinates $x_1,\dots,x_n$ on $\mathbb{C}^n$, $\mathcal{O}=\mathbb{C}\{x_1,\dots,x_n\}$ is the ring of convergent power series and $\mathfrak{m}=\langle x_1,\dots,x_n\rangle$. blocks.content:
arXiv:math/0603444v2  [math.AG]  31 Oct 2006
QUASIHOMOGENEITY OF ISOLATED HYPERSURFACE
SINGULARITIES AND LOGARITHMIC COHOMOLOGY
MICHEL GRANGER AND MATHIAS SCHULZE
Abstract. We characterize quasihomogeneity of isolated hypersurface singu-
larities by the injectivity of the map induced by the ﬁrst diﬀerential of the
logarithmic diﬀerential complex in the top local cohomology supported in the
singular point.

blocks.title: Relation to the logarithmic comparison theorem
blocks.content: The map $d_1$ is well-known in the context of the logarithmic comparison theorem: By Grothendieck's comparison theorem [@Gro66], the cohomology of the complement $U=\mathbb{C}^n\smallsetminus D$ of a germ of a reduced divisor $D\subseteq\mathbb{C}^n$ is computed by the complex $\Omega^\bullet(\star D)$. If the inclusion $\Omega^\bullet(\log D)\subseteq\Omega^\bullet(\star D)$ is a quasi--isomorphism then $\Omega^\bullet(\log D)$ computes the cohomology of $U$ and one says that the logarithmic comparison theorem, or briefly LCT, holds for $D$.
